title: DNA Extraction Using the Ammonium Acetate Technique
author: Juan Carlos Illera
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.knycvfw
materials: Move the supernatant to new tubes.

steps.title: Prepare blood‑DNA mixture
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL blood, 200 µL DNA extraction solution (containing 30 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8, 10 mM EDTA, and 0.4 % SDS), and 3 µL proteinase K to a tube.

steps.title: Vortex and incubate overnight
steps.instruction: Vortex briefly, then incubate the mixture overnight at 56 °C.

steps.title: Add ammonium acetate and mix
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL 4 M ammonium acetate, vortex, and incubate for 30 min, shaking the tube every 10 min.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 800 µL cold 100 % ethanol to the supernatant.

steps.title: Discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully remove and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70% ethanol
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet with 800 µL 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Dry pellet
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and allow the pellet to air‑dry.

steps.title: Resuspend in TE buffer
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL TE buffer to the dried pellet and incubate in an oven at 37 °C for 2–3 h.

steps.title: High‑temperature incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 70 °C for approximately 3 h, shaking frequently.
